readme_intent: ComparatorChallenges/README.md (665 bytes) says, in full: install `landrun`, `lean4export`, and `nanoda_bin` on PATH, then from the repository root run `lake exe cache get`, `lake exe comparator ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.json`, and `lake exe comparator ComparatorChallenges/Euler.json`; it thanks the Formal Conjectures authors for their Lean formalization of the Navier-Stokes problem statement 'which we adapted for these Comparator challenges'. The README itself does not define what is compared; that is defined by the Comparator tool it invokes (leanprover/comparator, pinned in lake-manifest.json at rev 19e111e2141cf333c7daff0f64c5f24acc91dd2e, checked out under .lake/packages/Comparator). Per that tool's README and Main.lean/Comparator/Compare.lean: a *challenge* module (here ComparatorChallenges.NavierStokes / ComparatorChallenges.Euler, importing only Mathlib, containing the target theorems with `sorry` proofs) is built and exported with lean4export inside a landrun sandbox; a *solution* module (NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution / Euler.Solution, 'provided by a party trying to convince you that they have proven' the theorems) is built and exported the same way; then for every name in `theorem_names` the tool requires (1) the exported ConstantVal (name, universe params, type term) of the theorem to be equal between challenge and solution, (2) every constant reachable from the statement's type (transitively through types AND definition values, via `runForUsedConsts`) to be identical as a kernel constant in both environments (so solution-side copies of the challenge definitions must match the challenge's exactly at the term level), (3) the solution proof to use no axioms beyond `permitted_axioms` (propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice), and (4) the solution environment to be re-checked by the Lean kernel (replay) and, with `enable_nanoda: true`, additionally by the independent nanoda kernel. A pass is the tool exiting 0 and printing 'Your solution is okay!'; any mismatch, illegal axiom, or kernel rejection throws and exits non-zero (test fixture simple_mismatch: exit_code 1). The party that runs it is whoever executes the command; nothing in the clone records that anyone has.

files.what_it_carries: Four-line instruction set (install landrun/lean4export/nanoda_bin; `lake exe cache get`; two `lake exe comparator <json>` invocations) plus an acknowledgement that the Formal Conjectures Navier-Stokes formalization was 'adapted' for the challenges. No hashes, no statement text, no expected output.

The Navier-Stokes challenge module. Header: 'Copyright 2026 The Formal Conjectures Authors ... modified from its original form'; docstring says 'Standalone comparator copied from' formal-conjectures commit 8bf45ed70d48b2b2a501de9c00b26bfa38c573ee FormalConjectures/Millenium/NavierStokes.lean with 'imports, metadata attributes, namespace, and local notation' adapted and utilities inlined; imports only Mathlib. Namespace NavierStokes.Comparator. Declarations: def divergence; theorems divergence_of_not_differentiableAt, divergence_zero, divergence_const, divergence_add, divergence_smul (proved); def IsOnePeriodic; structures InitialVelocityCondition, InitialVelocityConditionDecay, InitialVelocityConditionPeriodic, ForceCondition, ForceConditionDecay, ForceConditionPeriodic, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothness, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessPeriodic (all generic in dimension n); target theorems navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 (L273-277, alternative (C): ∀ nu > 0, ∃ u₀ f, InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ ForceConditionDecay f ∧ ¬∃ v p, NavierStokesExistenceAndSmoothnessRn nu u₀ f v p) and navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic (L280-284, alternative (D), same shape with the Periodic structures), both `:= by sorry`. 3 `sorry` tokens (2 proofs + 1 docstring mention).

Comparator config only: challenge_module ComparatorChallenges.NavierStokes, solution_module NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution, enable_nanoda true, theorem_names [NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3, NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic], permitted_axioms [propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice]. It records no hashes, no statement text, and no mapping beyond module/theorem names.

The Euler challenge module. Same Formal Conjectures copyright header; docstring says 'Adapted from FormalConjectures/Millenium/NavierStokes.lean at .../blob/main/...' (no commit pinned), 'specialized to zero viscosity and zero external force'; imports only Mathlib. Namespace Euler (not NavierStokes.Comparator). Declarations: def divergence (ℝ³ only); structures InitialVelocityCondition, InitialVelocityConditionDecay, EulerExistenceAndSmoothness, EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3; target theorem euler_breakdown_R3 (L85-88: ∃ u₀, InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ ¬∃ v p, EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 u₀ v p) `:= by sorry`. Then a second block (L90-184) that is NOT from Formal Conjectures — its docstring says it is 'the following version of EulerPacketInduction.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity', i.e. the project's own theorem restated: defs toL2, vorticity, velocityC1Norm, vorticityNorm; structures SobolevSmoothOn, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On; target theorem exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity (L170-184, a 12-conjunct existential over u₀, Tstar, v, p asserting compact smooth nonzero data, 0 < Tstar ≤ 1, a maximal Sobolev-class solution on Ico 0 Tstar with bounded energy, the closed-interval existence iff T < Tstar, locally finite C¹ norm and vorticity integral, limsup of C¹ norm = ⊤, vorticity integral = ⊤, and no global EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 solution) `:= by sorry`. 2 `sorry` tokens.

Comparator config only: challenge_module ComparatorChallenges.Euler, solution_module Euler.Solution, enable_nanoda true, theorem_names [Euler.euler_breakdown_R3, Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity], permitted_axioms [propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice]. No hashes, no statement text.

what_it_does_not_establish: That the comparator definitions are a correct formalization of the Clay (C)/(D) statements. Comparator only checks that the solution proves the same Lean proposition as the challenge; the meaning of that proposition (derivWithin on Ici 0 for the time derivative, ContDiffOn on univ ×ˢ Ici 0 for smoothness, MemLp (‖v · t‖) 2 plus a strict uniform bound ∃ E, ∀ t ≥ 0, ∫‖v‖² < E for finite energy, decay via iteratedFDerivWithin bounds, pressure periodicity per the Clay errata) is inherited from the Formal Conjectures authors' choices as adapted by the project, and is outside the comparator's scope.

Independence of the challenge from the proving party. Both challenge files carry the header 'modified from its original form' and were adapted by the project (namespace, notation, inlining). The Euler challenge is not a DeepMind statement at all: it is the project's own specialization (zero viscosity, zero force), and its second target theorem exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity together with toL2, SobolevSmoothOn, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On, vorticity, velocityC1Norm, vorticityNorm is explicitly 'the following version of EulerPacketInduction.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity' — authored by the project. For that theorem the comparator would compare the project's statement against the project's own restatement.

That the upstream Formal Conjectures definitions were copied faithfully. No upstream copy is present; the files cite three different pins (8bf45ed7…, 8323e878…, 'main'); a reviewer must fetch upstream at the cited commit and diff.

A kernel check. Nothing in the clone shows the comparator (or `lake build`) was ever run: no .lake/build, no comparator binary, no logs; formalization.yaml's review status is 'self-assessed'. Textual identity of statements and definitions (verified here) is necessary but not sufficient for Comparator's term-level equality, since elaboration depends on the import closure and instance resolution — the project itself had to add `attribute [local instance] CompletePartialOrder.toSupSet` (Euler/Solution.lean L41) to make the reference's ENNReal supremum elaborate the same way. Whether the two environments actually export equal terms is only known after running the tool.

That the proofs are sorry-free or use only the permitted axioms. The solution modules contain 0 `sorry` tokens at the top level, but the 580- and 1829-module import closures were not scanned for sorry/axiom declarations here, and `#print axioms` output requires a build.

Anything about how the witnesses are chosen. The comparator statements quantify ∀ nu > 0, ∃ u₀ f (NS) and ∃ u₀ (Euler). The project's bridge discharges (C) and (D) with zero initial velocity `fun _ => 0` and a viscosity-rescaled force `toComparator (rescaledForce ν f)` (NavierStokes/ComparatorR3Theorem.lean L30, NavierStokes/ComparatorTheorem.lean L38); this is permitted by the statement (and by the Clay text, which lets both u° and f be chosen) but the comparator says nothing about unforced or nonzero-initial-data Navier-Stokes. No quantifier mismatch between the submission and the challenge was found: the submission restates the challenge verbatim.

Correctness of the translation between the project's internal vocabulary (NavierStokes.ProblemStatement: time-first SpaceTime, VelocityField, spatialDivergence) and the comparator's (space-first curried functions, Comparator.divergence). That translation (NavierStokes/ComparatorBridge.lean, 253 lines; ComparatorR3Bridge.lean, 89 lines; Euler/*ComparatorBridge* modules) is part of the proof term and is checked only as a proof, not audited by the comparator as a statement.

Comparator's own trusted base: it assumes the challenge's import closure (here all of Mathlib at the pinned rev), the lakefile, the mathlib cache, landrun's sandbox, and at least one of the Lean or nanoda kernels are trustworthy (tool README, assumptions 1-6). The lakefile.toml in this clone sets `leanOptions = { autoImplicit = false, warningAsError = true }` only for the Euler lib; the NavierStokes and ComparatorChallenges libs use defaults.
gate_answer: Worked from source at clone HEAD 8937a8f4cbc7abaab5e9e97d1cc7f5d2319d9538. The ComparatorChallenges directory is the project's Comparator setup: two Mathlib-only challenge modules with sorry'd target theorems (NS: navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 / navier_stokes_breakdown_periodic in namespace NavierStokes.Comparator, adapted from Formal Conjectures commit 8bf45ed7; Euler: euler_breakdown_R3 and the project-authored exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity in namespace Euler), two JSON configs naming those theorems and solution modules NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution / Euler.Solution with permitted axioms propext/Quot.sound/Classical.choice and nanoda enabled, and a README that just says how to run leanprover/comparator. Everything the README intends that can be done from source PASSES: the challenge definitions are byte-identical to the project-side copies (NS 211 lines, Euler 96 lines), the four target theorem statements are byte-identical between challenge and solution, the solution modules state the theorems in terms of those copied definitions (ComparatorSolution.lean L16-26, Euler/Solution.lean L33-56) with no clashing declarations, and no module in the solutions' import closures (580 and 1829 project modules) imports a ComparatorChallenges module. What is NOT established: the comparator was never run here (comparator, landrun, lean4export, nanoda_bin absent; no build; no logs in the clone), so term-level statement equality, axiom footprint and kernel acceptance remain unverified — and the project's own `attribute [local instance] CompletePartialOrder.toSupSet` workaround shows textual identity does not by itself guarantee identical elaboration; the definitions could not be compared to the Formal Conjectures upstream (no copy, three inconsistent pins); and by construction the mechanism cannot say whether these definitions faithfully encode Clay (C)/(D), nor is the Euler challenge independent of the project (its second theorem and its definitions are the project's own restatement). The JSON files record no hashes or statement text, so the 'byte-for-byte against the JSON' check is inapplicable.
